source: swdl_boombox_6.5GT.iso NA 1.22.0.3, same hashes as prior sessions

physical_link.chip_selects: 2 (num_cs=2) -- confirms the SPI3 bus is shared between the two 78K0R microcontrollers (front controller + IOC), one per CS
physical_link.confirmed_boot_gating: waitfor /dev/spi3 blocks the rest of primary startup until the SPI driver is up; dev-ipc is started immediately after and everything else (touch/buttons/display backlight/CAN gateway/boot-mode) waits on dev-ipc's mount points

transport_layer.driver: /boot/bin/dev-ipc, VERSION 2.3.0 -- this is a generic, documented Harman 'ipc/spi driver' resource manager, NOT a Harley-specific protocol at this layer

args_decoded.-c8: 8 virtual channels multiplexed over the one physical SPI link
args_decoded.-M3 -C0: SPI module 3, SPI channel/CS 0 (the front controller; CS1 -- channel 1 -- is presumably the second 78K0R, not seen invoked separately in these scripts)
args_decoded.-D0x608: SPI mode word (polarity/phase/word-size bits, same style as the audio DSP's McSPI2 mode word found earlier)
args_decoded.-K1000000: 1 MHz SPI clock for this link (higher than the DSP's SPI0 6 MHz derivation, lower than max -- likely chosen for the 78K0R's slower peripheral clock)
args_decoded.-I136,137: two OMAP interrupt lines used as IPC_REQ / IPC_ACK handshake signals -- this means the link is NOT simple polled SPI; the 78K0R actively interrupts the OMAP to signal 'I have data' and 'I got your data', on top of the raw SPI clock/data lines. A software reimplementation MUST wire these two IRQs, not just bit-bang SPI.

transport_layer.flow_control: XON/XOFF flow control per channel, visible in dev-ipc's own diagnostic strings (rx/tx XOFF|XON counters) -- the link can be throttled per virtual channel independently
transport_layer.protocol_versions: dev-ipc supports IPC protocol V1.0 (default) and V2.0 via -p; which version this firmware actually negotiates was not confirmed (no explicit -p flag in any boot script, so it defaults to V1.0)
transport_layer.resulting_device_tree: /dev/ipc/ch0 .. ch7, /dev/ipc/onoff, /dev/ipc/watchdog, /dev/ipc/debug -- each is a plain QNX character device from userspace's point of view; dev-ipc handles all SPI/interrupt/flow-control plumbing underneath

confirmed_from_actual_usage_in_firmware.ch2: power/reset control -- the stock 'reset' utility does the entire reset request by writing 2 raw bytes (0x00 0x02) to /dev/ipc/ch2. This is the single simplest, most directly reusable fact in this whole session: `echo -ne '\x00\x02' > /dev/ipc/ch2` is a real, documented way to trigger a system reset through this link.
confirmed_from_actual_usage_in_firmware.ch3: front-panel buttons, touchscreen, and display backlight -- owned by iocInterface and SetDisplayBrightness. iocInterface also manages touch calibration (reads/writes EEPROM offset from mmap_eeprom.cfg's 'touchCal' field, 0x1874/28 bytes, found in the boot-path session) and posts key/touch events to /dev/faceplate for the rest of the system to consume.
confirmed_from_actual_usage_in_firmware.ch5: speech recognition front-end (started by the 'ndr' service) -- likely carries streamed audio or VR-button-press events, not confirmed further
confirmed_from_actual_usage_in_firmware.ch8: boot-mode negotiation -- ioc-boot-mode reads this channel at both normal boot and SWDL boot to ask the 78K0R which mode to come up in (letters mapped to codes 66/70/85 = 'B'/'F'/'U', matching the boot-path session's SWDL trigger condition)

channel_map.unconfirmed: ch0, ch1, ch4, ch6, ch7 -- allocated (8 channels total) but no script in this firmware exercises them directly; they may be used only from compiled services (audioCtrlSvc referenced /dev/ipc/ch2 as well per an earlier session's string dump, worth reconciling) or may be reserved/unused in this hardware variant.

front_panel_message_format_CONFIRMED_FRO.source: Verbatim comment block in the stock multipleKeyMaps.cfg, citing an internal spec by name: '//Harley/isys/iocontroller/trunk/doc/Harley IOC J3 IPC Interface.doc', Section 2.3.1.3
front_panel_message_format_CONFIRMED_FRO.meaning: This CONFIRMS a real, named internal protocol document exists (title: 'Harley IOC J3 IPC Interface'). We don't have that document, but the firmware comments quote its exact bit layout for the digital-keys field of the Front Controls IPC message:
front_panel_message_format_CONFIRMED_FRO.example_multi_key_decode: config line '0x0007=0x42' means bits 0,1,2 of byte5 (POWER+INT+COMM) held together maps to ASCII 'B'; this is purely a host-side software combo table, not something the 78K0R itself encodes -- the 78K0R just reports raw button-state bits per message, and iocInterface does the combo detection in software using this table.
front_panel_message_format_CONFIRMED_FRO.implication_for_a_replacement_OS: A replacement front-panel driver does NOT need to reverse-engineer combo/multi-key logic from the wire protocol -- it only needs the raw per-button bitmask from the 78K0R (bytes 5/6 as documented above) and can reimplement combo detection in software exactly like iocInterface does, using this same authoritative bit table.
